A sales representative should handle the three requests as follows:

1. **Immediate deletion:** Do not promise immediate deletion. Under official policy, data is removed from active access immediately but physical deletion takes up to 90 days after contract termination [NL-019-S05]. Custom deletion SLAs may be negotiated for Enterprise clients through a DPA, for example a 30-day active purge and 60-day backup purge, but these must be documented and approved with Priya Raman and legal [NL-019-S05] [NL-009-S08]. Always cross-reference the Security Policy for binding timelines [NL-009-S08].

2. **Teams availability:** Do not guarantee a launch date. The Microsoft Teams integration is in the planning and design phase for Q4 2026 and should be framed as a target, not a contractual commitment [NL-009-S08]. Do not offer custom, one-off builds or insecure "alpha" releases; engineering has confirmed no custom Teams bot builds or early production releases [NL-027-S04]. Sales representatives should stop telling prospects it is "almost ready" and instead offer the responsive mobile web interface as an interim workaround [NL-027-S04].

3. **Custom pricing:** Do not offer custom discounts on Starter or Growth plans; all discounts require Marcus Reed's approval and must align with the current pricing sheet [NL-009-S08]. Use only the 2026 pricing schedule, with Enterprise starting at $8,500/month and a minimum $15,000 implementation fee [NL-004-S05]. Do not quote final Enterprise pricing on discovery calls, and never use deprecated historical prices [NL-009-S08] [NL-004-S05].
